title: wb knowledge store configuration
description: Declares a repository's knowledge store and its protected-path set. A repo with no .wb-knowledge.json gets no enforcement at all: the guard hook is inert, so a marketplace install never denies writes in someone else's repository. Enforcement is fail-open ACROSS repos and fail-closed WITHIN a configured one.
$comment: THIS FILE AND THE CONFIG IT VALIDATES ARE CORE SELF-EXTENSION. Every control in the knowledge loop reads the config; if the loop could edit the policy deciding what needs human review, every other control would be bypassable in one move, and the bypass would read as a routine config change. Both files therefore appear in their own protected_paths, and the schema below requires that. Changing either is a human-only act, permanently, with no configurable override.

$schema.description: Path or URL to this schema.

version.description: Config format version. Bump only alongside a human-reviewed migration.

store.description: Where this repo's knowledge store lives.

branch.description: The long-lived store branch. Never merged into main; main merges forward into it. MERGE, NEVER REBASE — rebasing rewrites the commits that entry provenance SHAs point at, silently invalidating every stored reference.
branch.$comment: scripts/knowledge-worktree reads this to resolve the store checkout.

root.description: Directory on the store branch holding entries/, staging/, SCHEMA.md and the generated INDEX.md.

protected_paths.description: Paths, relative to the repo root, that an armed agent run may not write to. Directories end with '/'. This is the repo's declared core self-extension set: the machinery that evaluates or steers the system. Ambiguous cases are default-denied INTO this set rather than left out of it.
protected_paths.$comment: In a wb-development repo this covers the harness itself (commands/, agents/, skills/, hooks/, scripts/, .claude-plugin/) plus the steering documents (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md) and the promoted-entry tree. In a host project it would instead cover that project's own CLAUDE.md and .claude/ config. knowledge/staging/ is deliberately ABSENT: capture must be able to write there, and staging is ungated by design.

items.description: Repo-root-relative path. Must not start with '/' — absolute paths would not survive being read in a different checkout.

allOf.$comment: The config MUST declare itself. This is the trust anchor: the moment it is created is the moment the scheme becomes self-protecting, and a config that omitted itself would let the loop rewrite its own policy. Machine-enforced here rather than left to review.
The schema MUST be protected too. Protecting the config while leaving the schema writable would let the loop relax the rules the config is validated against — the same bypass, one level up.

write_policy.description: How knowledge entries may be promoted. Defaults to the strictest setting; when relaxed, it relaxes along ORIGIN — evidence — rather than along a self-assessed category a model could mislabel.
write_policy.$comment: DELIBERATE ABSENCE, DO NOT ADD: there is no 'core_self_extension' key here, and adding one would be a defect rather than a feature. All core self-extension is permanently human-gated with no configurable override; a configurable control over the control IS the bypass. The setting is not merely defaulted to off — it is unexpressible, which is why additionalProperties is false on this object and on the root.

ordinary_entries.description: Policy for ordinary knowledge entries — claims about the codebase. Never applies to core self-extension, which has no policy surface at all.

tool_verified.description: Entries derived from tool output: test results, diffs, validator verdicts, executed probes. This is the ONLY axis along which the policy may be relaxed, because it maps to evidence a tool produced rather than to a judgement the model made about itself.
tool_verified.$comment: v1 ships 'propose-only'. 'auto-promote' is designed but not exercised.

model_narrated.description: Entries derived from model narration — anything a model concluded, summarised, or inferred, including reading a file and reporting what it said. Always human-reviewed.
model_narrated.$comment: A const, not an enum with a default. Model-narrated content is exactly what the zombie-agent threat model describes: injected text that survives into memory and is legitimized as a learned pattern by the refinement process. There is no value of this field that permits automatic promotion, so none is offered.
